NoteFileStore.ReadAsync performs bounded strict UTF-8 decoding and fingerprinting; only after it returns are path/fingerprint/BOM/saved/editor fields replaced. Toggling undo clears prior-document history. Known file errors retain the existing document and give a generic 1 MiB/access hint. finally reenables controls. Native picker surfaces are explicitly outside capture-exclusion assurance.

blocks.title: Select save destination without treating dialog cancellation as success
blocks.explanation: Save refuses Present mode and concurrent file work. Existing document path/fingerprint are reused for ordinary Save; Save as or a new document opens a generic .txt SaveFileDialog with overwrite prompt. Cancel returns false before setting fileBusy. A newly selected destination resets expected fingerprint; the following block reads an existing destination before writing so replacement can still check for intervening changes.

blocks.title: Advance the saved baseline only after persistence completes
blocks.explanation: fileBusy disables editor changes and content snapshots the exact text being saved. Save-as/new overwrite reads the destination fingerprint, then NoteFileStore.WriteAsync verifies it around a same-directory temporary write. Successful return updates path/fingerprint/savedText. A NoteConflictException has its own Save as guidance; other known failures retain edits with an access/space/UTF-8/size message. finally always clears busy. The helper's checks are conflict detection, not an external-writer lock.

blocks.title: Keep note status generic and validate the full paste result
blocks.explanation: File failure classification covers IO/access/encoding/argument exceptions. SetFileBusy disables the editor and confirmation panel before recalculating actions. Dirty status reveals neither path nor note text and explicitly says no automatic saving. Paste obtains UnicodeText, constructs the post-selection replacement, and asks NoteFileStore.Fits to enforce strict UTF-8 bytes including any BOM; invalid/nontext/Present paste is cancelled, not truncated.

blocks.title: Change font and root tint without fading glyphs
blocks.explanation: Note font steps by two within 12..42. Background alpha is rounded from clamped 10..100 percent times 255/100 and assigned to WindowSurface.Background using current theme RGB; Window.Opacity and reading control opacity are untouched. ApplyTheme replaces resources, updates next-theme icon/name/automation text and Plain outline, then reapplies the existing slider value so switching palettes preserves tint strength.

blocks.title: Toggle notes without erasing them and find from current selection
blocks.explanation: Expanding Notes hides audio setup and collapses Q/A (which cancels/stops its provider); collapsing only hides Find. Wrap changes TextWrapping without changing content. Find opens the inline panel; Next rejects empty input, searches after the current selection with current-culture case-insensitive matching, wraps once to the beginning, and selects/scrolls the match or reports none. Visibility changes do not reset note text or undo state.

blocks.title: Route covered and armed-mode keys before legacy file shortcuts
blocks.explanation: Covered input first consumes hidden-workspace keys, allowing normal Tab, Alt+F4 and activation of the focused external mask toggle. It returns immediately after that cover decision. If the controller is active, the same window's preview event delegates key, modifiers and IsRepeat to HandleKeyboardKey, assigns its Boolean result to Handled and returns even when ordinary text editing is allowed through. Modal Edit can therefore retain text-control shortcuts without falling through to Notes Open/Save/New routing. No process-wide keyboard hook is involved.

blocks.title: Reserve Escape for question typing and shortcuts for global Edit
blocks.explanation: Outside the earlier covered/modal branches, Escape exits independent question typing and consumes the event. Other shortcuts are ignored unless exactly Control is held and presenting is false, so question typing during Present does not gain note Open/Save/New commands. Ctrl+S/O/N/F are marked handled and routed to their existing guarded asynchronous/file/find methods rather than duplicated implementations. This legacy path stays separate from the active controller's local command vocabulary.

blocks.title: Refresh Computer and Mic lists independently
blocks.explanation: Existing selected device IDs are saved before enumeration. Each successful list replacement reselects the same ID or the first available item, and empty lists provide mode-specific guidance. Separate catches let one discovery succeed when the other fails; the second status can supersede the first. This refresh does not substitute an input in an active session: RefreshDevices_Click below rejects active startup/running/stopping states.

blocks.title: Keep passive device choice local and audio tools inline
blocks.explanation: Refresh is blocked while starting, running or stopping. In Present, a click on an enabled device-row container assigns its Content directly to SelectedItem and consumes the preview event, avoiding the default focus-requiring ListBox click path. Audio setup toggles inline; opening it collapses Notes/Q&A but does not start audio. This is passive device choice, unlike direct transcript selection's deliberate typing transition.

blocks.title: Reject explicit Start before disturbing session state
blocks.explanation: Duplicate Start during busy/stopping/running returns immediately. Capture mode determines which selected device objects are required; protection, every requested input and a token length of at least 32 are prerequisites. Failure exposes audio setup with an Edit/token hint. The endpoint defaults to literal IPv4 loopback and must parse as absolute before audioBusy/session changes. Stronger loopback/path validation follows inside the try; URI parsing alone is not the network policy. A missing token expands the inline Service setup section so the existing setup guidance still leads to a visible password field.

blocks.title: Start a GUID-stamped capture with old partials archived
blocks.explanation: A local cancellation source is published so Stop can cancel startup; controls enter audioBusy before work. After ValidateEndpoint, the display buffer begins a session, a new capture GUID/timestamp is recorded, the structured store closes old partials and ArchiveTranscriptPartials materializes their history rows. StartAsync receives only selected device IDs, endpoint, token and that GUID. Known failures show generic startup guidance; finally clears the published token reference/busy flag before the using scope disposes it. Preparation is not rolled back into the old session.

blocks.title: Disable source changes throughout startup and stopping
blocks.explanation: Start requires idle plus protection; Stop is available while starting or running but disabled during stop. Both device lists and mode buttons use a shared idle predicate. Mode determines visible/enabled sections and label/border, while token entry additionally requires global Edit. SetCaptureMode repeats the busy guards, so directly invoking its handler cannot bypass disabled buttons; successful mode changes only reset meters and controls, never open inputs. UpdateRecordingIndicator reads transcriber.IsRunning on every controls refresh, so starting/buffering alone does not light the red icon and stopped/faulted state hides it.

blocks.title: Coalesce repeated stops and cancel startup before waiting
blocks.explanation: StopTranscriptionAsync returns the existing incomplete audioStopTask. Otherwise it sets audioStopping and disables changes, cancels any pending start token, then stores StopTranscriptionCoreAsync. The core awaits transcriber.StopAsync and records elapsed capture time; recognized connection/device failures warn that unfinished tail text may be missing. finally clears stopping, zeros both meters and recalculates controls, independent of whether stop reported an error.

blocks.title: Reject stale capture callbacks before mutating either transcript
blocks.explanation: A production event without CaptureSessionId becomes Guid.Empty; only diagnostics may borrow the current session for synthetic events. A mismatched GUID returns before logs or data updates. Accepted partial/final events update display/export buffer, then structured question state, then final/partial UI rows and placeholder. Finals require segment IDs. Known invalid data or capacity failures stop transcription and retain memory for export. Updates across the two stores are sequential, not a multi-store transaction.

blocks.title: Export one transcript snapshot without autosaving audio
blocks.explanation: Export requires global Edit, no file work and content; the native .txt picker is explicitly cancelable. Once busy, transcript.ExportText snapshots finals plus any unfinished labels. Existing destination fingerprint is read before bounded NoteFileStore.WriteAsync; only success advances exportedTranscript. Capture is not stopped by export, so later transcript changes can make it dirty again. Failure keeps in-memory text, and finally releases fileBusy. This exports text, not PCM.

blocks.title: Clear transcript only after full stop and saved export
blocks.explanation: Running, startup-busy and stopping states all reject Clear. Dirty transcript also rejects it with export-or-discard-at-exit guidance. Success clears display and structured stores, chooser and export baseline, then clears main rows under a selection-recursion guard and refreshes partials/placeholder. It intentionally does not call questionDraft.Clear: copied question text can outlive clearing the source transcript.

blocks.title: Serialize close requests and release window-owned subscriptions
blocks.explanation: Until allowClose is explicitly granted, WPF Closing is cancelled and at most one queued async Exit request proceeds. Its finally clears the queue guard even when a prompt keeps the window open. Closed unsubscribes system events, removes the HWND hook, unregisters hotkeys, stops diagnostic health and sets answerProviderClosing before awaiting visible-activity and transcriber disposal. Application.Shutdown is explicit after cleanup; this differs from Hide.

blocks.title: Set up a synthetic UI harness without enabling inference
blocks.explanation: RunUiSmokeAsync creates its output directory, forces diagnostic rendering and invalid SnapshotOnly provider state, then reveals through the normal protection path. It measures foreground/native passive state, Start availability, default notes collapse and Both selection. The token is cleared and endpoint counts recorded. Documentation mode replaces displayed device names with synthetic fixtures; constructor enumeration already happened, but no capture start is implied.

blocks.title: Populate synthetic source rows and inspect local cursor/nonactivation
blocks.explanation: Fixed notes plus Computer/Mic finals and partials exercise the real ReceiveTranscript path using diagnostic session fallback. Source labels must appear in both row collections. After rendering, transcript-primary geometry is checked. Native WM_MOUSEACTIVATE and WM_SETCURSOR messages verify MA_NOACTIVATE and Arrow policy along with control cursor properties. These messages cannot establish that a remote recorder includes or excludes the cursor.

blocks.title: Check theme bindings and preserve original content/handle baselines
blocks.explanation: The harness snapshots note/export/HWND and iterates every UiTheme, checking actual dynamic resource colors and note/transcript reading brushes against ThemePalette. It renders each theme, tests Plain-to-dark-to-light button transitions/icons, restores DeepSeaFoam and renders audio setup. These are specific brush/state assertions; they do not compute all contrast ratios over arbitrary backgrounds.

blocks.title: Exercise passive Computer and Mic device-row clicks
blocks.explanation: Two synthetic devices replace each real enumerated ItemsSource temporarily. After layout, a preview mouse event on the second container must change selection without making the row focusable or changing foreground/Keyboard.FocusedElement. Original list and selection are restored after each source. This tests the shared passive handler against actual realized WPF containers, not device capture or real pointer automation.

blocks.title: Use busy/stopping negative controls before any audio can start
blocks.explanation: Computer and Mic modes must enable/hide the corresponding device sections. With audioBusy=true, attempting a mode change must retain Both. With audioStopping=true, invoking Start, mode change and Clear must leave the export unchanged and Start/mode controls disabled. These flags deliberately simulate transitional states; the assertions do not require or prove WASAPI startup/shutdown behavior.

blocks.title: Sample low/full root alpha and check solid foregrounds
blocks.explanation: The fixture renders at 10% and 100%, converts a transcript background point through current DPI and reads one Pbgra32 pixel alpha. It requires a nonzero low alpha below 60, opaque alpha 255, full control/window opacity, opaque foreground brushes and unchanged HWND. Reset to 55 follows sampling. A local RenderTargetBitmap is evidence about the WPF visual tree only, not screen-capture exclusion.

blocks.title: Exercise notes expansion, internal scrolling and native hit regions
blocks.explanation: Notes expansion must keep presenting true. One hundred synthetic transcript rows drive an internal vertical scroll, then the real row collection/highlights are restored under the render-selection guard. A long unwrapped note tests horizontal scrolling before text/wrap restoration. WM_NCHITTEST samples must return caption=2, left resize=10 and client=1 at the editor, separating drag/resize from text interaction.

blocks.title: Check global mode permissions and block busy document replacement
blocks.explanation: The real presentation toggle must enable note editing on request and restore read-only/nonfocusable Present while leaving the tint slider enabled. Repeated mode/Notes visibility transitions must preserve notes/export. Setting fileBusy and pending New then executing must leave both note and pending action intact. Finally minimizing and RevealAndReset must restore a normal visible-state window after protection reapplication.

blocks.title: Force URI rejection before transport or device work
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic substitutes a Computer device and synthetic 64-character token so missing-input/token guards do not mask the URI branch. It temporarily sets an invalid URI, invokes Start_Click and throws unless the inline invalid-address status appears. finally restores environment, clears the token, restores device items/selection and returns to Both. This tests early validation only, not endpoint connectivity.

blocks.title: Combine synthetic subdiagnostics and close even on failure
blocks.explanation: Question, answer, clarification and recording-indicator diagnostics are awaited; each throws on failed assertions before final receipt generation. The outer passed expression combines shell/layout/theme/guard checks, tool-window style and no running capture. result.json includes individual booleans, API readback, discovered counts, fixture mode and an explicit no-real-audio/no-remote-cursor-guarantee limitation. Return is zero or two; finally grants close regardless of success. Recorded invalidUriRejected=true is justified by the preceding throw-on-failure branch. Audio-device-card checks cover paging/selection, busy locks, empty state and compact Service setup. Cover checks include continued fake work and fresh-tree versus cached accessibility limits. The newly awaited keyboard diagnostic then checks modal routing, identity selection, explicit submission, font/device behavior and recovery; its result is included as keyboardChecks, and failure throws before the outer receipt rather than being silently ignored by its older aggregate expression.

blocks.title: Render WPF content locally and pack native hit-test coordinates
blocks.explanation: RenderDiagnosticAsync updates layout, yields to Render priority, scales dimensions by actual DPI and renders the window into Pbgra32 before PNG encoding to the requested file. It is not a screenshot of the user's desktop. HitTestDiagnostic converts a WPF point to screen pixels and packs signed-coordinate low/high 16-bit fields for WM_NCHITTEST; SendMessage/GetForegroundWindow declarations support the synthetic native assertions.

files.role: Applies and checks the shared Windows arrow cursor only in the app's owned-window cursor-message path.

blocks.title: Load a shared Arrow handle and reject native load failure
blocks.explanation: The static Arrow value uses LoadCursor with null instance and integer resource 32512. A zero handle throws Win32Exception using the preserved last error instead of silently using a missing cursor. SetArrow assigns this handle and IsArrow compares current cursor handle for diagnostics. MainWindow.WindowMessage calls SetArrow for its own HWND; no ShowCursor loop or global cursor visibility modification exists here.

blocks.title: Declare the narrow user32 cursor boundary
blocks.explanation: LoadCursorW requests last-error preservation because loading can fail. SetCursor and GetCursor use native pointer-sized handles; the code does not inspect another process or manipulate a recording product. The loaded system cursor is shared rather than created by this class, so no owned-cursor destruction path is declared.

files.role: Provides session-local instance ownership and a narrow same-user REVEAL recovery channel without accepting arbitrary text, paths or executable commands.

blocks.title: Derive a per-user name and acquire local-session ownership
blocks.explanation: Current Windows user SID is required, hashed with SHA256 and shortened to 24 hex characters for the pipe/mutex suffix. The mutex name has the Local namespace prefix; IsOwner follows whether this invocation created it. The pipe itself uses the SID-derived name, while CurrentUserOnly is applied by streams below. The hash names the channel; it is not an authentication secret or a universal cross-session mutex guarantee.

blocks.title: Send only REVEAL and start one listener
blocks.explanation: A nonowner creates a same-machine, output-only, asynchronous CurrentUserOnly client. Connect/write/flush share a five-second cancellation source and exactly six UTF-8 command bytes. Listen rejects nonowners and a second listener, then stores the async loop task. App.OnStartup supplies dispatcher-marshalled callbacks, so the IO loop need not manipulate WPF controls on its own thread.

blocks.title: Read a bounded command from one same-user connection
blocks.explanation: The loop creates one input-only byte-mode server instance with CurrentUserOnly. After connection, a linked two-second request timeout bounds ReadExactlyAsync into a six-byte buffer. Only those bytes matching REVEAL invoke the callback; any other six-byte value gets a generic rejection. The implementation does not inspect trailing bytes beyond the command, so it should not be described as validating the peer's entire stream.

blocks.title: Separate listener shutdown from peer timeout and connection failure
blocks.explanation: Cancellation caused by shutdown exits quietly; other cancellation reports a request timeout and accepts another connection. IOException reports a generic recovery failure and delays 250 ms before retrying to avoid a tight error loop. That delay also observes shutdown. These error messages reveal no incoming bytes, user SID, note content or file path.

blocks.title: Release the owner mutex without disposing a live listener token
blocks.explanation: Dispose is idempotent, cancels listener work, releases the mutex only for its owner, then disposes the mutex handle. If no listener exists it disposes shutdown immediately; otherwise a default-scheduler continuation disposes it when the task ends. This avoids disposing the cancellation source beneath pending pipe IO and does not block application exit waiting synchronously for a dispatcher callback.

files.role: Registers and releases this window's explicit Ctrl+Alt recovery, Notes Edit and configurable keyboard-control hotkeys without a keystroke hook.

blocks.title: Record only successfully registered hotkey IDs
blocks.explanation: The primary constructor captures the HWND. IDs1,2and3 identify visibility, global Notes Edit and keyboard control separately from their virtual keys. MainWindow supplies Space/E for recovery/edit and the validated configured key for control. Register always combines Control, Alt and NoRepeat bits; it neither installs a global letter hook nor allows arbitrary modifier policy. Native failure throws immediately with last error, and only success appends the ID for cleanup. The caller handles conflicts, retaining the Keys button and second-launch recovery rather than claiming registration always succeeds.

blocks.title: Attempt every unregister and keep cleanup diagnostics generic
blocks.explanation: Dispose walks successfully registered IDs and calls UnregisterHotKey on the captured handle. A failed unregister emits a generic Trace warning but does not prevent later IDs being attempted; clearing the list makes another Dispose harmless. Both interop declarations preserve last error and marshal Win32 BOOL; only registration uses last error to throw.

files.role: Applies native tool-window/nonactivation styles and capture affinity, retaining readback uncertainty rather than converting API success into a recorder guarantee.

blocks.title: Require a supported desktop and obtain a hidden-capable HWND
blocks.explanation: ProtectionResult records readback availability, nullable affinity and error separately. Constants identify extended styles and WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE=0x11. Configure refuses Windows earlier than build 22000, calls EnsureHandle without needing Show, checks DWM HRESULT and composition state, and throws if unavailable. MainWindow controls visibility/order; this native helper does not load notes or independently hide the window. DisallowPeek is the documented DWM attribute11, distinct from capture affinity0x11.

blocks.title: Preserve other style bits and distinguish missing from contradictory readback
blocks.explanation: The existing extended style is read-modify-written: ToolWindow added, AppWindow removed, NoActivate set or cleared by the requested interaction mode. SetWindowPos uses no-size/no-move/no-zorder/no-activate plus frame-changed flags. Affinity setter failure is fatal; successful getter with a value other than 0x11 is also fatal. Getter failure alone is retained in ProtectionResult. DwmFlush submits composition synchronization, not independent recipient-capture qualification. The same HWND also receives DWMWA_DISALLOW_PEEK=true as a32-bit BOOL. A failing HRESULT follows the existing hidden protection-failure path. PeekPreventionRequested means setter acceptance, not observed shell preview or universal capture exclusion.

blocks.title: Handle zero native return values correctly across process bitness
blocks.explanation: Get/SetWindowLongPtr are used for 64-bit and Get/SetWindowLong for 32-bit. Last error is cleared before each call because a zero old style/value can be legitimate; only zero with a nonzero last error throws. The 32-bit write checks conversion to int instead of silently truncating. FlushComposition maps DwmFlush's HRESULT to a managed exception.

blocks.title: Declare the exact user32 and DWM contracts
blocks.explanation: Pointer-sized and 32-bit entry points are separate imports with last-error preservation. Affinity and SetWindowPos return Win32 BOOL and are explicitly marshalled; DwmIsCompositionEnabled returns HRESULT plus a marshalled Boolean, and DwmFlush returns HRESULT. These signatures express local API setup only: they neither inspect a sharing application's backend nor verify captured pixels.

files.role: Declares the Windows WPF executable and its Core/audio dependencies; build metadata does not qualify the resulting UI or package.

blocks.title: Select the desktop executable target and manifest
blocks.explanation: Microsoft.NET.Sdk plus UseWPF makes App.xaml/MainWindow.xaml compiled WPF resources/code. WinExe selects a GUI executable, net10.0-windows and EnableWindowsTargeting identify the platform target, and ApplicationManifest points to app.manifest. AssemblyName is PhantomFudge and declared package/assembly version is 0.1.0. Repository Directory.Build.props supplies nullable/implicit-usings/warnings/determinism/lockfile settings; nothing here demonstrates a build was run.

blocks.title: Reference the domain layer and the external audio package
blocks.explanation: The ProjectReference makes Core models, file store, answer adapters and policies available to the WPF app. NAudio is pinned at 2.2.1 and used by the Audio subdirectory, a different atlas ownership boundary. The package's internal implementation and lockfile are not interpreted by this desktop annotation; this block states the declared dependency, not device compatibility.

files.role: Translates Core's semantic color strings into WPF resources, including control system-color overrides and the separate high-contrast reading role.

blocks.title: Replace semantic resource brushes from a single palette
blocks.explanation: Apply reads ThemePalette.For(theme), maps each color field to the matching Theme resource name, and replaces resource entries with frozen brushes. The palette Name is presentation text, not a brush. HighContrastReading is distinct from ThemeText so white/black reading text can coexist with canonical muted/chrome colors. DynamicResource consumers in App/MainWindow XAML observe these replacements; arbitrary hardcoded brushes would not follow this mapping.

blocks.title: Align built-in colors and freeze parsed brush instances
blocks.explanation: System control/window/highlight/gray resource keys point at the same semantic objects, keeping framework-rendered pieces coherent with custom templates. Color uses WPF ColorConverter; Brush constructs a SolidColorBrush and freezes it before returning, so theme switching replaces immutable instances rather than mutating shared ones. MainWindow calls Color separately when constructing a per-slider alpha background.

files.role: Shows the active transcription state as a protected red icon and exercises its presentation without opening audio inputs.

blocks.title: Map active transcription to an inline recording icon
blocks.explanation: The partial window uses WPF visibility and the existing palette. The small setter makes the icon Visible only for the supplied running state and Hidden otherwise. Hidden retains its layout slot, so recording transitions do not move Start/Stop. Production calls it from UpdateAudioControls with transcriber.IsRunning; it does not infer recording from sound levels, partial text or the chosen Computer/Mic/Both mode.

blocks.title: Check stopped, starting and active presentation without audio
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic saves busy/status/theme state and first requires no running transcriber and a hidden icon. It models startup with audioBusy=true, refreshes production controls and requires the dot to remain hidden. Only the view setter is then driven with true across all themes, checking visibility, exact theme-error brush, solid opacity and12by12dimensions. No capture object is started or its Running field changed.

blocks.title: Render a disclosed synthetic example and restore state
blocks.explanation: The example uses the original theme and an explicit SYNTHETIC status saying no inputs opened. After visual-tree rendering, false must hide the icon. finally restores busy/status/theme and refreshes controls even if rendering fails. The aggregate also requires the real transcriber to remain stopped. A failed assertion throws; recordingStarted=false describes the fixture, not a hardware recording experiment.

files.role: Coordinates measured card rows and source-independent overflow pages while preserving endpoint selection.

blocks.title: Observe source collections without replacing selected objects
blocks.explanation: Each source owns an independent page index, capacity and reveal-selection flag. Collection and generated-container events queue layout after the actual records exist. The lists and their selected endpoint objects remain the source of truth; the helper owns only presentation. These listeners are attached to controls owned by this window, not global device hooks.

blocks.title: Coordinate the setup workspace and selected-page reveal
blocks.explanation: Only a true visible transition outside cover and keyboard-mode switching closes Notes and Q/A and asks each list to reveal its selection. A parent hide does not recursively reenter the question-edit transition. Service setup toggles inline, while size and selection changes request a reflow. A selection marks only that source's page for reveal; no input is opened by any of these handlers. Cover host swaps and the controller's protected hide/reveal must not accidentally take the Q/A close/cancel path. Normal explicit audio-setup opening retains that path; the switching guards are not a general cancellation bypass.

blocks.title: Coalesce layout work and keep source modes separate
blocks.explanation: A queued flag and arranging guard prevent recursive reflow while dimensions or visibility are changing. Work is dispatched at Loaded priority and skipped while the setup panel is closed or not initialized. The group grid uses two columns for Both and one for a single source; empty-state notices and each independent list's layout are then refreshed. finally releases the arranging guard on every path.

blocks.title: Measure friendly-name cards within real viewport dimensions
blocks.explanation: Unrealized or very small/invisible lists wait for a later layout rather than using bogus dimensions. Columns derive from a190-unit target; width reserves margins. FormattedText measures wrapped friendly names with actual font/DPI, starting at68units high and adding content padding. The height is bounded by available space, so exceptionally long names may use the template's ellipsis without altering identity. Unexpected item types fail explicitly.

blocks.title: Compute finite pages without losing hidden selections
blocks.explanation: The calculation first tests capacity without a pager, then reserves32units only when pages are needed. Capacity is columns times whole rows and never zero. RevealSelection maps the existing selected index to its page; otherwise the current page is clamped. The label also shows where the selected device lives. Paging changes container visibility/geometry only, preserving ItemsSource and SelectedItem even when that card is temporarily hidden.

blocks.title: Reject browsing while capture lifecycle locks inputs
blocks.explanation: Output and microphone arrow handlers route to their own page objects. Disabled lists, startup, stopping or active capture reject navigation with an inline message. An accepted arrow changes only a page index and reflows cards, never selects another device automatically. Direction comes from the two declared button tags; there is no model or audio transport interaction.

files.role: Exercises actual no-scroll card templates and source selection using synthetic device records only.

blocks.title: Settle WPF geometry and reject hidden scrolling or clipped cards
blocks.explanation: The diagnostic performs three bounded layout/queued-update passes. Its geometry predicate rejects any ScrollViewer in the device-list template, checks every visible card's edges against the list, and requires at least one visible card for a nonempty collection. It checks container fit, not that arbitrary-length device names can always be displayed without ellipsis.

blocks.title: Populate a disclosed large synthetic device catalogue
blocks.explanation: The fixture saves original selections, sources, size, mode, status and theme. It substitutes23playback and17microphone records, selects the first of each and opens setup with service details collapsed. Minimum, medium and large viewports must keep visible cards inside both lists and keep the lists themselves reachable. No capture device is constructed or started.

blocks.title: Page without selecting, then explicitly select a card
blocks.explanation: At minimum size the Next action must advance the output page while retaining the previously selected object. A synthetic preview click on the first visible card then selects that exact output, leaves the microphone unchanged and preserves passive foreground behavior. Every theme must render the selected card's actual accent border; the compact screenshot is synthetic evidence only.

blocks.title: Cover capture locks, single-source layouts, service setup and empty lists
blocks.explanation: A busy flag disables both lists and paging and must reject a navigation attempt. Computer-only and Mic-only views use a full-width source column while retaining identity. Expanded service details must remain usable without card scrollbars. Empty catalogues must show explicit messages and remove pager strips; absence is not fabricated into a selectable default device.

blocks.title: Restore controls and report only synthetic scope
blocks.explanation: finally restores dimensions, original item sources/selections, mode/status/theme, closes setup and restores Q/A even if a check fails. The aggregate requires all geometry, selection, style, lock, mode, service and empty-state checks plus a stopped transcriber. It writes a local receipt and throws on failure; audioCaptured=false documents that this fixture never opened real inputs.

files.role: Swaps the workspace for a plain cover without stopping ongoing transcription or answers, while narrowing fresh UI Automation traversal.

blocks.title: Start uncovered and keep a single explicit toggle
blocks.explanation: The partial window tracks only visual cover state, prior keyboard focus and a transition guard. InitializeCover detaches the unused CoverView so the initial visual and automation tree contains the normal workspace. The top-bar button toggles this state; there is no recorder detection, startup recording or implicit model request.

blocks.title: Refuse unsafe cover entry and disarm local commands
blocks.explanation: Repeated/reentrant state changes return. Entering cover is refused while file I/O, unsaved confirmation or protection recovery is pending, preserving actionable UI. If keyboard control is active, LeaveKeyboardControl runs before the cover-switching guard is set, restoring passive interaction and attempting the controller's foreground return. That mode transition can temporarily hide/reprotect/reveal the window, but it does not invoke the real Hide action's audio/provider shutdown. Covered content must not remain in an armed local command mode.

blocks.title: Detach the actual workspace while retaining its ongoing work
blocks.explanation: Inside the guarded transition, cover entry remembers focus only when it belongs to WorkspaceRoot, clears keyboard/logical focus, disables the workspace and detaches it before attaching CoverView. This is not a paint-only overlay: the normal visual/logical host is empty while covered. Named controls, models and asynchronous audio/answer work remain alive. The swap itself issues no stop, cancel, provider reconfiguration or new request; disarming keyboard mode was handled before entering this branch.

blocks.title: Restore the visual tree and rebuild the window's automation children
blocks.explanation: Uncover removes CoverView and restores/enables WorkspaceRoot. The icon remains unchanged; a two-unit border marks covered state and accessible names describe showing the notepad or restoring the workspace without visible text captions. ResetChildrenCache synchronously rebuilds the window peer children, then invalidates peer state. Cached references and retained memory remain outside this fresh-tree improvement. finally releases the transition guard.

blocks.title: Resume layout and visible timing without restarting work
blocks.explanation: After the transition guard is cleared, uncover recalculates layout, queues existing device-card layout and renders the latest answer. Prior keyboard focus is restored only if the element is still visible, enabled and focusable, and never during synthetic rendering. Nothing restarts audio or resubmits a question; text received while covered is already in the retained controls/models.

files.role: Exercises synthetic cover appearance, retained background work and explicitly limited accessibility-tree privacy.

blocks.title: Gate a fake answer until the cover is active
blocks.explanation: The fake provider signals acceptance without yielding text, then waits on an explicit release gate with the actual request cancellation token. It yields one synthetic delta and terminal completion. This arrangement proves a response can arrive after cover activation without contacting a model, and makes erroneous cancellation observable.

blocks.title: Traverse an existing WPF automation peer tree with a bound
blocks.explanation: A queue walks GetChildren from the window peer and refuses more than4096peers. The test can compare references obtained before and after detachment, rather than treating hidden pixels as accessibility proof. This is in-process provider traversal, not a cross-process screen-reader certification.

blocks.title: Establish meaningful before/after accessibility controls
blocks.explanation: Synthetic note/question text and the delayed provider create content worth hiding. The pre-cover tree must contain the editor peer. A simulated audio-start token/busy flag makes accidental shutdown detectable. Cover must detach visual and logical parents, disable the workspace and hide its fields. Fresh traversal must omit old note/question/answer peers while retaining the cover message and toggle. A separate cached-value probe records whether a saved peer still reads retained text, explicitly exposing the limitation.

blocks.title: Continue transcript and answer work without false visible timing
blocks.explanation: The cover blocks an accidental workspace shortcut. A current-session synthetic transcript final arrives and the fake answer is released; completion, unchanged original draft/note/source/session and an uncancelled start token are required. No extra snapshot is created. First-visible logging must remain false while detached. All themes must keep the cover label/toggle visible and omit synthetic private values from fresh traversal.

blocks.title: Inspect real cover-message pixels, minimum geometry and unchanged HWND
blocks.explanation: The synthetic WPF render is sampled within the actual DPI-scaled text bounds; more than100bright pixels prove the message was drawn rather than trusting IsVisible alone. Minimum-size geometry must leave the message/toggle visible. HWND/styles/protection remain unchanged through cover. Uncover must restore the answer text and ordinary editor traversal and then record its first visible assignment.

blocks.title: Preserve editing and device setup and refuse file-busy cover
blocks.explanation: The fake audio-start guard is cleared before further UI checks. Independent question editing survives a cover cycle. Audio setup also restores its selected output/microphone objects without visibility callbacks closing it or reconfiguring work during host swaps. File-busy activation is rejected. Synthetic content/provider mode is then cleared and normal fixture state restored.

blocks.title: Report bounded evidence rather than universal invisibility
blocks.explanation: The aggregate requires visual, keyboard, background-work, fresh accessibility, compact, HWND, restoration and busy-guard checks. The receipt separately reports cachedPeerValueReadable, zero live model requests and no audio capture. Its limitation explicitly excludes cached external clients, process inspection and recipient capture qualification. Failed checks throw instead of generating a successful privacy claim. The final aggregate also requires an accepted native Peek-prevention request; actual taskbar-hover output is not tested.

blocks.title: Assert the icon-only top-left mask target
blocks.explanation: The helper checks that button content is the actual vector Path with geometry, not a string caption. Its top-left coordinates must stay within the header inset, and its target remains32by32. Native hit testing at its center must report client content rather than caption dragging. Covered and restored modes both run this assertion; the separate drag check moved to an unobstructed header point.

files.role: Keeps an explicit session-only answer font choice stable across responsive layout and gives compact action captions full accessible names.

blocks.title: Distinguish an unset preference from a user-selected size
blocks.explanation: The nullable chosenAnswerFontSize starts unset, allowing layout to supply its automatic size until the user chooses. Slider events are ignored before answerViewReady and while the code itself is synchronizing the slider; otherwise the double value is rounded to an integer and sent through the shared setter. This state belongs to this window instance, with no settings-file persistence. Only answer/interpretation typography is controlled here, not transcript, question or Notes font sizes.

blocks.title: Validate before committing a session preference
blocks.explanation: SetAnswerFontSize rejects values outside KeyboardCommands' inclusive 8..24 bounds before changing the stored choice. An accepted value becomes the preference, updates the text/slider pair and recalculates workspace layout so a larger reader can receive space. Invalid direct callers receive ArgumentOutOfRangeException instead of silent clamping. Commands already validate their numeric payload in Core; this second guard protects the UI setter independently.

blocks.title: Apply responsive defaults without overwriting explicit choices
blocks.explanation: ApplyAnswerFontSize chooses the stored preference over the caller's automatic size, writes AnswerText.FontSize and updates the slider only if it differs. updatingAnswerFont suppresses the resulting ValueChanged callback and is reset in finally, preventing a programmatic compact-layout default from becoming a user preference. AdjustAnswerFont starts from the currently displayed size, adds the requested delta and clamps to the same 8..24 endpoints before committing through the setter. Resize therefore preserves a chosen size while untouched windows can retain their 9/10 automatic policy.

blocks.title: Shorten captions without losing action meaning
blocks.explanation: After readiness, a QuestionPanel width below 560 selects shorter Cancel/Copy captions. Provider preparation counts separately from an active answer: only unfinished preparation without AnswerBusy uses the preparation wording. The request's unconfirmed clarification flag distinguishes copying an interpretation from an answer. AutomationProperties always carries the full action name even when the visible caption is shortened. These assignments change labels only; enabled-state, cancellation and clipboard behavior remain in the existing answer handlers.

files.role: Moves an independent keyboard cursor across existing device cards and pages, committing an endpoint only on explicit Space while capture is idle.

blocks.title: Start navigation from the selected endpoint without selecting another
blocks.explanation: keyboardDeviceList and keyboardDeviceTarget represent navigation, not the actual capture selection. Microphone-only mode starts on MicrophoneDevices; Computer and Both start on OutputDevices. The target is the list's existing SelectedItem or, when none is selected, its first item. BeginKeyboardDevices then reveals that target without assigning SelectedItem, opening an audio endpoint or issuing Start. An empty list leaves a null target for the explicit empty-state path.

blocks.title: Reveal the cursor page independently of the selected card
blocks.explanation: ClearKeyboardDeviceCursor removes tags from realized containers in both source lists. Reveal acts only in Devices mode with a current list; an absent target produces an inline no-device hint. For a valid target it disables selected-card page snapping, sets the page index from target index and page capacity, runs the existing measured card layout, and tags the realized target KeyboardCursor. The hint reports source and one-based cursor position. Container styling shows this navigation border without rewriting endpoint identity or claiming that the target is selected.

blocks.title: Refuse navigation during capture and switch source only in Both mode
blocks.explanation: Startup, stopping, running capture or a disabled/missing list consumes the key with a stop-first hint before any target or selection change. Tab switches the navigation list only when captureMode is Both, starting from that source's selected item or first available item; it does not change captureMode. Empty lists are handled before indexing. These are runtime guards in addition to the command that enters Devices mode, so a later capture-state change cannot leave browsing enabled.

blocks.title: Clamp row, card and page motion; reserve selection for nonrepeated Space
blocks.explanation: The column estimate uses the same 190-unit target as card layout. J/Down and K/Up move by a row, left/right by one card, and bracket/Page keys by the current page size. Long arithmetic before clamping avoids overflow from a large page capacity; the nonempty-list guard makes the final index valid. Only Space with repeated=false assigns SelectedItem. Movement and repeated Space merely update/reveal the cursor, preserving the chosen endpoint and never starting transcription. Unrecognized keys are consumed with zero movement in this modal handler.

files.role: Navigates and filters transcript rows by structured identity while keeping the cursor, copied question selection and explicit submission separate.

blocks.title: Enter selection with an identity cursor, not an implicit selection
blocks.explanation: The cursor stores TranscriptSegmentKey, independently of the copied draft entries. A source filter, local search string and pending first-g flag are separate navigation state. Begin first checks eligibility, resets filters and the g sequence, opens Q/A and its reading view, then enters Select and points at the last matching row. Refresh/reveal updates presentation only; no row is automatically copied, frozen or submitted. The last row may be a live partial because the row sequence appends current partials after retained finals.

blocks.title: Protect edited drafts and filter raw segment text
blocks.explanation: CanKeyboardSelect requires protection, no file operation, no user-edited draft and no clarification lock; distinct inline hints explain the refusal instead of replacing the user's text. MatchesKeyboardTranscript requires a real Segment, compares the structured source when filtered, and searches segment.Text with OrdinalIgnoreCase. Labels and session separators are not parsed as content or identity. KeyboardTranscriptRows materializes final/history rows followed by live partials, while the hint counts all copied draft entries, including any currently hidden by the filter.

blocks.title: Filter collection views without changing transcript storage or copied selection
blocks.explanation: Refresh installs the same predicate on both list collection views only while Select/Search is active and the question view is ready. renderingTranscriptSelection suppresses SelectionChanged mutations while filtering hides rows; finally releases the guard, then SyncTranscriptSelection projects retained draft keys into the visible lists and the cursor is retagged. Reset removes both filters under that same guard and reconciles highlights again. Neither operation deletes transcript records or drops selected copies just because they are temporarily outside the view.

blocks.title: Keep cursor styling and scrolling separate from selected rows
blocks.explanation: UpdateKeyboardTranscriptCursor tags only realized items whose full segment key matches the cursor while Select/Search is active; other tags are cleared. This does not set IsSelected or transfer WPF keyboard focus. Reveal finds the same key in each current list view, requests ScrollIntoView and updates the hint. Recognition refresh can therefore retag a replacement partial/final row without selecting the newest incoming line; explicit navigation is what requests reveal/scroll here.

blocks.title: Apply local search while retaining a still-visible cursor
blocks.explanation: Find trims the search string, returns from Search to Select and refreshes the view. If the old key still matches, it remains the cursor; otherwise the first matching key, or null for no matches, replaces it. The empty-result hint explains clearing the search with an empty submission. Search changes neither copied draft entries nor provider input: it is a local case-insensitive substring filter over the retained structured rows, combined with the current source filter.

blocks.title: Review with Enter and toggle copies only with explicit nonrepeated Space
blocks.explanation: The handler computes the current visible-row index and tracks adjacent unmodified g presses without counting held-key repeats as a fresh first g. Slash/F3 opens search; nonrepeated Enter enters Edit for review, not submission. Number keys change the source filter and rerun the existing search without clearing copied selections. Empty rows return a hint before indexing. Space ignores repeats, missing cursor and failed eligibility, then calls the shared ApplyTranscriptSelection with exactly one add or removal according to the draft's key membership. This preserves Core's one-session/count/text guards and does not freeze or call a provider.

blocks.title: Move within bounded visible rows without chasing incoming speech
blocks.explanation: J/Down and K/Up move one row, Page keys move five, Home/End choose endpoints, Shift+G chooses the latest visible row and the completed gg sequence chooses the first. Arithmetic is clamped to the already-checked nonempty row set. Only a nonnegative resulting index publishes a new structured cursor key and reveals it; other keys are consumed without creating a selection. Repeated navigation is permitted, unlike Space or submission. Incoming callbacks do not invoke this navigation switch, so a stable existing cursor does not automatically advance with new speech.

files.role: Coordinates deliberate window-local keyboard modes, guarded command dispatch and best-effort foreground return without using the global Notes editing shutdown transition.

blocks.title: Separate armed mode, copied-row navigation and native transition state
blocks.explanation: The controller distinguishes Inactive, Control, Select, Edit, Read, Command, Search, Devices and Help rather than interpreting letters whenever the window exists. KeyboardSelecting includes Search so entering its text prompt retains selection-layout and submission restrictions. Foreground HWND/PID, last eligible editor, prior prompt mode and three transition/action flags serve different purposes; none is an audio/provider lifetime token. Initialization loads shortcut settings, listens for both transcript lists' generated containers to retag their cursor and initializes a hidden or active bar. It does not register the native shortcut until the main HWND exists.

blocks.title: Disable only the activation shortcut when configuration or registration fails
blocks.explanation: LoadKeyboardShortcut accepts an injected loader for synthetic failure cases; production uses the Core loader and its validated allowlist. IOException, InvalidDataException, unauthorized access, argument and JSON failures all replace settings with a disabled shortcut and a generic Keys-button notice rather than aborting window construction. Accessible naming reflects the resulting configured chord or disabled state. Registration is skipped in diagnostics and for disabled settings; a Win32 collision records a separate fallback notice without disabling local Keys interaction. Registration uses the settings' validated VirtualKey rather than parsing arbitrary key names in WPF.

blocks.title: Enter only after protected recovery and retain a bounded foreground-return target
blocks.explanation: The Keys click and native hotkey share one toggle. An already active mode leaves immediately; a file operation or pending confirmation refuses new entry. The previous foreground HWND is captured before TryReveal can activate the app, but entry still stops if protection is unavailable. Successful recovery uncovers the workspace and records only an other-window handle plus its process ID, then enters Control and surfaces any shortcut notice. This is deliberately not TogglePresentationAsync: it does not request audio shutdown, answer cancellation or global Notes editability.

blocks.title: Change local modes without equating temporary hiding with stopped work
blocks.explanation: Edit entry rejects file work, absent protection and a clarification-locked original question unless a reply is awaited. switchingKeyboardMode brackets Hide/reprotect/reveal when the old passive policy differs from the requested mode, preventing deactivation/visibility callbacks from treating that internal transition as a user shutdown. Leaving Select/Search restores the unfiltered view; remaining inside refreshes it, and non-Devices modes clear candidate tags. Controls/bar update before reveal, the flag clears in finally, and layout/editor/device setup follows. Nondiagnostic focus then targets the prompt, eligible editor or inert command sink; no branch here invokes Ask, Stop or provider cancellation.

blocks.title: Recover an asynchronously replaced Edit target without reclaiming external foreground
blocks.explanation: Outside Edit the remembered target is cleared. Inside Edit, AwaitingClarificationReply chooses the reply or original editor and its visible label, but a hidden, disabled, nonfocusable or read-only candidate becomes null. Refresh records identity even in diagnostics; actual Focus requires a changed nonnull target, no internal mode/cover transition, valid protection and a visible active window. This repairs the asynchronous interpretation-to-reply transition while refusing to steal focus back after the user switched applications. UpdateAnswerControls invokes it after clarification controls have been updated.

blocks.title: Restore passive policy before a best-effort foreground handoff
blocks.explanation: Leave is idempotent when inactive. It saves the old return identity, suppresses activation while SetKeyboardMode restores Inactive, clears stored identity and keyboard focus, and can explicitly skip foreground restoration for deactivation/exit or diagnostics. Otherwise it compares the current process ID for the saved HWND, checks IsWindow and attempts SetForegroundWindow. Failure reports that the user may need to switch manually; neither Windows foreground permission nor universal handle-identity safety is promised. The suppression flag is restored in finally even if the mode transition fails.

blocks.title: Abandon stale armed state without revealing an invalidated or hidden surface
blocks.explanation: Abandon directly clears active mode, independent question editing and foreground identity, then restores transcript filtering/device tags and the bar. Unlike Leave it does not perform a protected reveal or foreground transfer; callers use it for real Hide, global Notes transitions or invalidation before their own shutdown path. A genuine nondiagnostic window deactivation instead calls Leave without foreground restoration, unless mode/cover code caused the event itself. This prevents local letter commands from staying armed after switching to another application without making ordinary deactivation an audio-stop action.

blocks.title: Display modal affordances and curated suggestions without executing prompt text
blocks.explanation: The bar exists only while active; its TextBox appears only for Command/Search, and Edit labels distinguish original question from clarification reply. Hints describe each mode's actual review, navigation and explicit-submit path. Opening a prompt remembers the prior mode, changes mode and clears old text. Only Command TextChanged calls Core Suggest; no matches or an argument error becomes a local hint, while search typing remains inert until confirmation. Suggestions and help are built-in vocabulary, not model completions or shell dispatch. The stored prior mode later gives Command Escape its cancellation destination.

blocks.title: Prioritize native Alt handling, bounded Escape and explicit prompt confirmation
blocks.explanation: Inactive handling returns false immediately, and Alt combinations are left to normal window behavior. Escape is consumed but only a fresh press transitions: Control leaves, Search returns to Select, Command restores its prior mode, Devices closes setup, and other modes return to Control. Command/Search Enter is likewise nonrepeated and confirms the current prompt rather than falling into question submission. Command Tab inserts only the first curated suggestion and moves the caret; it never executes it. Other prompt keys return false for ordinary TextBox editing, with Core argument errors shown locally.

blocks.title: Require review before sending while preserving literal Edit input
blocks.explanation: After prompt handling, exact Ctrl+Enter is consumed and acts only on a nonrepeat: selecting asks for Enter review, while Control/Edit use the existing question/reply submission path. Other modes do not submit. Edit then returns false for all remaining input, preserving newline, letters and text-control paste instead of interpreting command keys. Outside Edit, other Control/Windows combinations are consumed; colon/F2 opens commands and F1/Shift-question opens Help once. Select and Devices dispatch to their own cursor handlers only after these global-in-the-window escape/submit/help rules.

blocks.title: Allow repeatable reading motion but not repeatable mode actions
blocks.explanation: Read delegates J/K/arrows, page and endpoint keys to the existing answer TextBox and adjusts its bounded font with plus/minus. All Read input is consumed here, including keys with no reading action, and repeat is intentionally allowed for scrolling/size changes. For the remaining modes, a held-key repeat returns before V/I/A/M can transition. Fresh V starts guarded transcript selection; I/A expand the existing Q/A reader before Edit/Read; M uses the explicit mask path. No case synthesizes pointer movement, selects transcript text implicitly or invokes a provider merely to enter a mode.

blocks.title: Reuse guarded submission and reject invalid command text before leaving the prompt
blocks.explanation: Question submission selects the clarification-reply handler only when a reply is awaited; otherwise it calls the existing Ask handler and displays its status. Command submission first parses the entire prompt with the Core grammar. An ArgumentException leaves the mode and text in place for correction and shows the validation message, so shell-shaped or otherwise unsupported input has no dispatch side effect. Only a valid typed KeyboardCommand returns to Control and reaches ExecuteKeyboardCommandAsync. The controller does not duplicate snapshot creation or provider-request construction.

blocks.title: Guard shared command dispatch and require idle devices or clarification state
blocks.explanation: Commands reject reentrant dispatch, file activity, pending confirmation and unavailable protection before setting keyboardActionBusy. Start delegates to the existing async-void click handler, whereas Stop awaits shutdown; the flag therefore protects this dispatch scope, not the full lifetime of every downstream operation. Source changes reuse SetCaptureMode's guards. Devices additionally refuses audio startup/stopping/running or an answer in progress before exposing setup; Clarify refuses an active answer before changing its toggle. Confirm likewise delegates to the established clarification handler, preserving its own state validation rather than creating a second confirmation implementation.

blocks.title: Delegate only typed built-ins and release the dispatch guard on every exit
blocks.explanation: The remainder of the switch handles validated numeric font/opacity values, three semantic theme aliases and explicit copy/clear/cancel/ask/mask/help actions. Clipboard access occurs only through the existing Copy handlers when those commands are deliberately executed; merely typing or completing a suggestion does not copy. Existing question/answer handlers remain responsible for their own busy/content guards and report their statuses. Unknown enum values throw instead of becoming arbitrary execution, and finally resets keyboardActionBusy even when a delegated action fails. The parser, not this dispatch switch, supplies valid argument/value shapes.

blocks.title: Disarm before masking and constrain native interop to foreground identity
blocks.explanation: MaskFromKeyboard leaves the controller before applying the existing cover behavior, so detaching the workspace cannot retain armed letter commands. Cover continues to own its separate visual/accessibility and background-work semantics. The three declarations support only best-effort foreground transfer, HWND validity and owning-process comparison; there is no cursor-warping API or global key hook here. Native return values are checked by Leave rather than interpreted as a guarantee that another application's presentation has regained focus.

files.role: Exercises keyboard-mode routing, draft identity, asynchronous edit targets and answer/device layout using injected failures, synthetic transcript rows and fake providers rather than real input or inference.

blocks.title: Inject configuration failures without touching the user's shortcut file
blocks.explanation: The fixture captures the original dimensions and accumulates named Boolean checks. Injected InvalidDataException, JsonException, unauthorized-access and argument failures must all leave the shortcut disabled with a fallback notice, covering the non-IOException invalid-data case explicitly. A default settings object then restores fixture state without rewriting keyboard.json. The UI is labeled synthetic and normal diagnostic initialization suppresses native hotkey registration. This verifies the load-failure boundary through its factory seam, not real disk permissions or operating-system shortcut collisions.

blocks.title: Prove activation and stable selected partials with a synthetic cancellation sentinel
blocks.explanation: A computer final and microphone partial enter the current transcript session before a disposable token marks synthetic audio startup busy. Direct activation must remove native no-activate style while keeping Notes read-only. A constructed WPF preview V event exercises the window-local router, and fresh then repeated Space must yield exactly one selected row with Ask disabled and no Edit transition. Finalizing the microphone partial must preserve the full cursor key and update that selected draft row to final; adding the computer row must compose both sources in transcript order. No capture source is opened by these assignments.

blocks.title: Check filtered cursor stability and compact review without creating a snapshot
blocks.explanation: Incoming unselected speech must not move the cursor or change two copied selections. Mic-only filtering hides computer rows without deleting their copied membership; local text search narrows to the finalized partial while leaving questionSnapshotCount unchanged. gg/Shift+G test endpoints. At minimum dimensions Select must borrow the reader, retain questionExpanded intent and leave the synthetic audio token uncancelled. Ctrl+Enter remains review-gated; plain Enter changes to Edit, restores all transcript rows and still creates no snapshot. Literal letters, newline and Ctrl+V must return unhandled for the editor rather than execute commands.

blocks.title: Submit exact text once and keep malformed commands local during fake streaming
blocks.explanation: The editor receives an exact CRLF-containing draft, and an injected SyntheticCoveredAnswer replaces any live provider. Fresh and repeated Ctrl+Enter must create only one new snapshot and pass the exact text into its recorded run. After leaving Edit, Read plus and a typed font14command must synchronize answer font and slider. A shell-shaped start string must remain in Command mode, leave capture stopped and preserve the already-streaming fake run. The screenshot records the command surface before execution; it is not evidence of an actual keyboard hook or model request.

blocks.title: Separate masking from cancellation using a releasable fake answer
blocks.explanation: After escaping the invalid prompt, M must cover and disarm into passive policy. Calling the activation toggle again must uncover into Control; the check name hotkeyUnmasks describes the shared entry point, not a real registered-hotkey event. Releasing the fake provider must complete its known answer text while audioBusy remains set, the synthetic startup token is uncancelled and the transcript session is unchanged. This proves that these local transitions preserve the fixture's work state without claiming any real capture or external foreground behavior.

blocks.title: Verify explicit maximum font survives responsive and passive layouts
blocks.explanation: The fixture sets the slider to24and checks minimum,900x600and1240x760viewports after layout settles. Answer text, font slider and Ask must remain reachable, with per-size layout receipts and a minimum-window screenshot. Leaving modal control at minimum size must retain both the chosen font and reachable reader in passive mode, then reentry resumes Read. Plus at24and minus at8must clamp rather than exceed the range. These checks exercise explicit font persistence across responsive mode changes; they do not establish readability on every display scale or measure real user typography.

blocks.title: Protect edited drafts and follow asynchronous clarification editor replacement
blocks.explanation: Attempting selection after manual editing must leave Control and the exact draft intact. Synthetic audio-busy state is cleared before the separate device fixture. A fake clarification provider then receives a question and, after asynchronous interpretation plus dispatcher settling, Edit must target the reply editor with EDIT REPLY. Awaiting answerTask alone can precede the interaction refresh queued by RunAnswerAsync's finally; ApplicationIdle waits for that UI turn instead of manually changing mode to repair the target. Fresh/repeated correction submission must record one unconfirmed request with exact reply text; a subsequent yes must record the confirmed third request. After the async transition settles again, the stored target and label must return to the original question editor. These are target-identity assertions in diagnostic mode, not real foreground-focus qualification.

blocks.title: Restore fixture state and fail the receipt when any named assertion is false
blocks.explanation: Escape from Control must restore inactive/passive state and the native no-activate bit; inactive V must remain unhandled. Normal completion restores dimensions, clears the explicit font/draft, removes the injected provider and returns answer configuration to snapshot-only before writing keyboard-controls.json. The aggregate uses every named Boolean and throws with the receipt when any is false. Its explicit limitation excludes real shortcut collisions and cross-application foreground return, and reports no captured audio or model calls. Main-fixture cleanup is on this normal path rather than a finally; the enclosing diagnostic harness closes the window if an earlier assertion or operation throws.

blocks.title: Navigate synthetic paged devices without selecting or starting capture implicitly
blocks.explanation: The helper saves both ItemsSource objects and selections, substitutes thirty fake output records and one fake microphone, and enters Devices through the parsed built-in command. Right must move the candidate while selected output stays0; only Space changes it to1. Paging must preserve that selection and fit without scrolling, while Tab changes the active source list. The busy-state branch receives Space on the sole, already-selected microphone: its assertion checks unchanged selection and stopped capture, not rejection of a different endpoint candidate. Escape must hide setup and return Control. No endpoint IDs are opened, and these exact assertions should not be read as hardware or native key-delivery tests.

blocks.title: Restore real device list references even if a synthetic device check fails
blocks.explanation: Unlike the main fixture's normal cleanup path, the device helper uses finally around all substitutions and navigation. It clears its artificial audioBusy flag, restores the original list objects and selected records, and collapses the setup panel even if settling, a command or a check throws. Restoring object references preserves real endpoint identity rather than reconstructing selection from a friendly name. The helper assumes the caller intentionally cleared busy state before entry; it is not a general live-capture state checkpoint.
